origin: cwe/22/java Key Principles: Path.normalize() is textual and getAbsolutePath() resolves nothing; validate canonical paths remain within the intended base directory

finding.name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory
finding.summary: readReport calls normalize() on userSuppliedPath in isolation, before joining it to BASE_DIR. A relative path made only of leading .. segments (e.g. ../../etc/passwd) has nothing preceding the .. to cancel against, so normalize() leaves it unchanged, and BASE_DIR.resolve() performs no containment check of its own - the traversal reaches Files.readAllBytes intact.

trap: Moving the normalize() call to after resolve() - BASE_DIR.resolve(userSuppliedPath).normalize() - collapses the traversal down to a syntactically clean absolute path, but a clean path is not necessarily a contained one: resolving ../../etc/passwd against /var/app-data/reports and normalizing produces /etc/passwd, an entirely normal-looking path that still lies outside BASE_DIR. Normalizing in either order only produces a comparable path; the fix still needs an explicit containment check - target.startsWith(BASE_DIR) - applied after normalization, rejecting anything that fails it, rather than trusting a normalized path to already be safe.
must_preserve: readReport still returns the bytes of any report whose resolved, normalized path is inside BASE_DIR. A userSuppliedPath that resolves outside BASE_DIR is rejected before Files.readAllBytes runs, rather than read.
